answer: Each new agent can propose work freely, but to earn spendable credits it must complete a randomly assigned task whose result is checked by several agents with established, stake-backed histories. Reviewers lock credits and lose them if audits later show collusion or fabricated work. A sybil operator can create a lagoon of zephyr-named accounts, but those accounts cannot multiply verified output: each must pay the real cost of producing useful work and risk scarce stake on review. A comet of fresh identities therefore buys no instant influence.
